summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of end-stage renal disease, diabetes, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation/flutter, and polysubstance use, was admitted for substernal chest pain radiating to the left shoulder and shortness of breath. The symptoms began after increased activity and were associated with dizziness. Initial concerns for acute coronary syndrome were ruled out with serial troponins showing no significant rise and EKGs demonstrating nonspecific changes. His chest pain resolved with medical management, including oral Percocet and optimization of beta-blockade. Shortness of breath was attributed to volume overload from excessive fluid intake after hemodialysis and uncontrolled hypertension, with imaging showing mild interstitial edema. He underwent scheduled hemodialysis, which improved his respiratory status, allowing weaning from supplemental oxygen. Hypertension and tachycardia were managed by continuing and titrating up labetalol. Hyponatremia on admission was corrected for hyperglycemia and resolved with fluid restriction. Medication changes included discontinuation of calcium acetate due to hypercalcemia, with initiation of lanthanum and Nephrocaps. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to adhere to fluid and sodium restrictions, monitor weight, and follow up with his primary care provider.
